New Study Suggests AI Chatbot Could Assist Doctors in Clinical Diagnostics

28 Oct 2026, 01:14 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Tech Desk · Source: blog.google

1 min read

Key takeawaysSource: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/health/amie-clinical-study-lancet/

Image: blog.google · Photo source · Cropped to 16:9; original source image

In this article
  1. AI Research in Primary Care
  2. Key Findings
  3. Future Implications

AI Research in Primary Care

A study published in The Lancet, led by researchers at Google and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC), suggests AI may support physician workflows. In a clinical trial involving 98 patients, the diagnostic AI chatbot, AMIE, gathered patient information before urgent care visits.

Key Findings

Supervising physicians reported that AI-generated summaries assisted preparation in 75% of cases and influenced care approaches in over 50%. The AI's differential diagnoses aligned with clinical outcomes 90% of the time, with no safety interruptions recorded.

Future Implications

While researchers emphasize that larger trials are necessary to confirm scalability, these findings indicate potential for AI to ease healthcare burdens and aid patient-physician interactions. Readers can review the full study methodology and safety data directly through the official publication.
